:::{#exr-r-squared-slr}
#### $R^2$ and the correlation

Assuming $S_{xx} > 0$ and $S_{yy} > 0$ (@def-centered-sums),
use @exr-rss-ols-fit to write the
[coefficient of determination](#def-r-squared) $R^2$ of the OLS fit
in terms of the
[Pearson correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-pearson-r) $r$,
and show that $0 \le R^2 \le 1$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-r-squared-slr}

The [total sum of squares](#def-tss) is $S_{yy}$ (@def-centered-sums),
and @exr-rss-ols-fit gives the residual sum of squares, so:

$$
\begin{aligned}
R^2
&= 1 - \frac{\text{RSS}(\est{\vth})}{\text{TSS}}
&& \text{(definition of $R^2$)}\\
&= 1 - \frac{\text{RSS}(\hintcoef, \hcoef{x})}{\text{TSS}}
&& \text{(the OLS estimate is $(\hintcoef, \hcoef{x})$)}\\
&= 1 - \frac{\text{RSS}(\hintcoef, \hcoef{x})}{S_{yy}}
&& \text{(TSS is $S_{yy}$)}\\
&= 1 - \frac{S_{yy} - S_{xy}^2 / S_{xx}}{S_{yy}}
&& \text{(residual sum of squares of the OLS fit)}\\
&= 1 - \paren{\frac{S_{yy}}{S_{yy}} - \frac{S_{xy}^2 / S_{xx}}{S_{yy}}}
&& \text{(split the fraction)}\\
&= 1 - \paren{1 - \frac{S_{xy}^2 / S_{xx}}{S_{yy}}}
&& \text{($S_{yy} / S_{yy} = 1$)}\\
&= 1 - 1 + \frac{S_{xy}^2 / S_{xx}}{S_{yy}}
&& \text{(distribute the minus sign)}\\
&= \frac{S_{xy}^2 / S_{xx}}{S_{yy}}
&& \text{($1 - 1 = 0$)}\\
&= \frac{S_{xy}^2}{S_{xx} S_{yy}}
&& \text{(divide a fraction by $S_{yy}$)}\\
&= \paren{\frac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} S_{yy}}}}^2
&& \text{(write as a square)}\\
&= r^2
&& \text{($r = S_{xy} / \sqrt{S_{xx} S_{yy}}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $-1 \le r \le 1$
([range of the correlation coefficient](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#thm-pearson-r-range)),
$0 \le r^2 \le 1$.

:::
